transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it’s really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... I guess I came in because, well, people have been pointing out some things about how I've been acting lately. I hope it's okay that I'm here for this, it's probably not a huge deal, but... they say they can actually see me moving like I’m, I don't know, like I'm underwater? Like it takes me forever just to answer a simple question or even get up out of a chair. 

And then other times, I'm just pacing around my apartment and rubbing my hands together, kind of like I’m trying to shake off a really bad customer service call. I don't mean to make a big fuss out of it, but my friends were getting a little worried. Is... is that the kind of thing that's helpful for you to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Are you currently taking, or have you recently started, any antipsychotic medication?

No, I'm not taking anything like that. I haven't started any new medications at all, actually. Um... I usually just try to power through things, you know? I don't really like taking pills if I don't absolutely have to. I hope that's okay. Is it... is it bad that I'm not taking anything? I just didn't want to mess up my system or anything, but if you think I should be, I'm completely open to it. Whatever you think is best, really.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or intensely energetic lately?

No, no, nothing like that. I haven't felt... high or super energetic at all. If anything, it's kind of the opposite, honestly. I've just been feeling pretty down and, you know, sluggish, like I mentioned. 

I definitely haven't had any of those really intense, up-and-at-'em kind of days. I hope that's the right answer? I mean, I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so you can figure out what's going on. Is it normal to not feel that way?
Have you been hearing voices that other people can’t hear?

Um... well, it's not like, you know, crazy voices telling me to do bad things or anything like that. I really don't want you to think I'm losing my mind. It's just... sometimes, I guess I hear work stuff when I'm not working. 

Like, my laptop will be completely closed, right? And I'll hear the little beep from my old headset, or... or I'll hear this voice that sounds exactly like one of my supervisors. They'll just say my name, or sometimes they'll say "too slow." Even when there's no phone ringing and I'm just sitting by myself. 

It's probably just stress from the job, right? Like my brain is just stuck in customer service mode. I mean, it's really not a big deal, I know it's not real when it happens. Is... is that what you mean? I hope that doesn't sound too weird.
Have you had any recent medical or neurologic illness?

No, no, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or in the hospital or anything. Physically, I'm... I'm actually pretty healthy. I try to take good care of myself, you know? I definitely haven't had any head injuries or weird nerve things... at least, nothing I've noticed. 

I hope that helps? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can do your job. Is it... is it a good thing that I haven't had any physical stuff going on? I'm assuming that rules some bad things out, right?
Has there been a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing that supervisor’s voice even though you were not feeling noticeably depressed or unusually up?

Um, well... yeah, I guess so. There have been times, like a few weeks here and there, where I actually felt pretty okay. Like, my mood was closer to normal, and I was getting my chores done, running errands, just being productive, you know? 

But... even during those good weeks, I would still hear that supervisor's voice sometimes, or... or I'd get this really strong feeling that the old ticketing software was flagging my account for being too slow. Even though I felt fine otherwise. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound worse. It's just... I want to be completely honest with you so you have all the facts. Does that make sense? Like, is it normal for that to happen even when I'm not feeling down? I hope I'm answering this the right way for you.
Have you ever had a period when you felt abnormally energetic or needed much less sleep than usual?

No, no, I've never had anything like that. I've never been, like, bouncing off the walls or staying up for days. I actually really value my sleep. I try to get a solid eight hours every night, you know, to be ready for work the next day. 

Sometimes I might have a little trouble falling asleep if I'm stressed, but I've never felt like I just didn't *need* sleep. I'm usually pretty tired by the end of the day. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to reassure you that I don't have any of those extreme energy swings or anything. I'm generally pretty steady in that department, I promise.
Have the voices or the feeling that your work account was being flagged been going on for longer than one month?

Um, well... yes. It's definitely been longer than a month. I hope it's okay to admit that. If I'm being completely honest—because I really want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details so you can help me—it's actually been going on for about a year and eight months. 

I know that sounds like a really long time, but I promise I've been doing my best to handle it! I try really hard not to let it get in the way of my job or anything. But yeah, the voice and that feeling about the tracking, they've been around for about that long. And it's not just when I'm going through the absolute worst of the sadness, either. It just sort of... hangs around, even when my mood is mostly fine. 

I really hope that doesn't make my situation sound too... you know, too severe or anything. I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly. Is that the kind of detail you needed?
Was there ever a full month when the voice or the feeling that your work account was being flagged was happening, but you were not feeling depressed at all?

Um... no, not a whole month. I mean, I've had those good weeks, like I mentioned, where I felt mostly okay and the voice was still there. But... it's never been a full month of just totally feeling fine while that stuff was happening. 

I really try to stay positive, you know? But the sadness does creep back in eventually. It's never stayed away for a whole four weeks while the other things were going on. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture. Is it okay that it hasn't been a full month? I'm trying really hard to get better, I promise.
Did the voice or the feeling that your work account was being flagged go away completely within one month after it first started?

Oh, um... no, they definitely didn't go away that quickly. I know I mentioned this just a little bit ago, but, um, the voice and the feeling about the tracking... they've actually been happening for about a year and eight months now. 

I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking! But yeah, they didn't just stop after a month. They've kind of just... stuck around all this time, even when I'm not in the middle of a really bad bout of sadness. I've really been trying to manage it all, though, so it doesn't affect my work too much. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
